'''Frank Günther Neese''' is a [[Germans|German]] [[theoretical chemistry|theoretical chemist]] at the [[Max Planck Institute for Coal Research]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.kofo.mpg.de/en/research/molecular-theory-and-spectroscopy|title=Molecular Theory and Spectroscopy|website=www.kofo.mpg.de|accessdate=16 December 2021}}</ref> He is the author of more than 440 scientific articles in journals of Chemistry, Biochemistry and Physics. His work focuses on the theory of magnetic spectroscopies ([[electron paramagnetic resonance]], [[magnetic circular dichroism]]) and their experimental and theoretical application, local pair natural orbital correlation theories, spectroscopy oriented [[configuration interaction]], electronic and geometric structure and reactivity of transition metal complexes and [[Metalloprotein|metalloenzymes]]. He is lead author of the [[ORCA (quantum chemistry program)|ORCA]] [[quantum chemistry]] computer program.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Neese|first1=Frank|year=2012|title=The ORCA program system|url=https://doi-org.proxy2.library.illinois.edu/10.1002/wcms.81|journal=WIREs Computational Molecular Science|volume=2|pages=73–78|doi=10.1002/wcms.81|s2cid=62137389|url-access=subscription}}</ref> His methods have been applied to a range of problems in [[coordination chemistry]], [[homogeneous catalysis]], and [[bioinorganic chemistry]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Neese|first1=Frank|year=2009|title=Prediction of molecular properties and molecular spectroscopy with density functional theory: From fundamental theory to exchange-coupling|journal=Coordination Chemistry Reviews|volume=253|issue=5–6|pages=526–563|doi=10.1016/j.ccr.2008.05.014}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Cox|first1=Nicholas|last2=Pantazis|first2=Dimitrios A.|last3=Neese|first3=Frank|last4=Lubitz|first4=Wolfgang|year=2013|title=Biological Water Oxidation|journal=Accounts of Chemical Research|volume=46|issue=7|pages=1588–1596|doi=10.1021/ar3003249|pmid=23506074}}</ref>

==Early life and career==
Neese was born on 13 December 1967 in [[Wiesbaden]]. He received both his Diploma (Biology – 1993) and Ph.D (1997) working with Peter M. Kroneck at the [[University of Konstanz]]. Neese performed postdoctoral work at [[Stanford University]] with [[Edward I. Solomon]] from 1997 to 1999, then returned to Konstanz where he completed his [[habilitation]] in 2001.{{Citation needed|date=May 2021}}

== Independent career ==
He joined the [[Max Planck Institute for Bioinorganic Chemistry|Max Planck Institute (MPI) for Bioinorganic Chemistry]] in 2001 as a group leader, where he directed a research group until accepting the position of full Professor and Chair of Theoretical Chemistry at the [[University of Bonn]] in 2006. In 2008, Neese returned part time to the MPI as one of its rare "Max Planck Fellows" within the Department of Inorganic Chemistry. In 2011, he became Director of the MPI for Bioinorganic Chemistry, renamed in 2012 in [[Max Planck Institute for Chemical Energy Conversion|MPI for Chemical Energy Conversion]], where he heads the department of Molecular Theory and Spectroscopy. In 2018 he moved to Mülheim's other Max Planck Institute, [[Max Planck Institute for Coal Research]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2021}}

==Personal life==
He is married to [[Serena DeBeer]], a spectroscopist who is a director of the [[Max Planck Institute for Chemical Energy Conversion]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2021}}

==Awards==
In 2005, Neese received the Hellmann Award of the German Theoretical Chemical Society for the Development and Application of new Theoretical Methods and subsequently the [[Klung Wilhelmy Science Award|Klung-Wilhelmy Weberbank Award]] in 2008 and the [[Leibniz Prize|Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz Prize]] of the [[German Research Foundation]] (DFG) in 2010. In 2013, he was inducted into the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]]. He was Associate Editor (2011–2014) of the journal [[Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics|''PhysChemChemPhys'']] and is a Member of the [[International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science|International Academy of Quantum Molecular Sciences]] (IAQMS, since 2012).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.iaqms.org/members/neese.php|title=International Academy of Quantum Molecular Science|website=www.iaqms.org|accessdate=16 December 2021}}</ref> Since 2015 Frank Neese has served as an Associate Editor of the journal ''[[Inorganic Chemistry (journal)|Inorganic Chemistry]]'' and as of 2016 he is Member of the Editorial Board of the review book series ''Structure and Bonding''. As of 2016 Neese has been appointed as an active member of the International Advisory Board for the Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry (IOCB) of the [[Czech Academy of Sciences]] in [[Prague]] and he was elected as a new Member of the Review Board "Physical and Theoretical Chemistry" in the field of "General Theoretical Chemistry" of the [[German Research Foundation|DFG]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2021}}
